scope: First-wave public-source findings, two matched mechanism comparisons, a conditional same-robot-access entrant scenario and structural comparators. Not a completed campaign or calibrated ownership-effect estimate.

evidence.claim: GXO and Agility announced a multi-year RaaS deployment of Digit and Arc at a SPANX facility following a late-2023 proof-of-concept. The stated workflow moves totes from AMRs to conveyors.
evidence.observation_period: Pilot late 2023; commercial deployment announced June 2024
evidence.locator: Opening three paragraphs and paragraph beginning In the SPANX facility
evidence.limitations: Customer/operator announcement corroborates named commercial setting, not independent performance. Robot count, revision, fees, title, SLA, uptime, staffing, duration in years and training rights are undisclosed. First-in-industry claim not independently validated.

evidence.claim: GXO discloses fixed-price closed-book/hybrid and cost-plus open-book contracts. Fixed components generally cover warehouse, technology and equipment; variable components relate to volumes and labor. Actual-cost deviations affect fixed-price profit; cost-plus reimburses allowable cost plus a specified margin.
evidence.locator: Item 7, Business Overview, paragraph beginning Our business model is asset-light
evidence.limitations: Company-wide contractual description; no basis to assign one of these customer contract forms to SPANX. Specified margin need not be a percentage. Contract detail does not identify realized automation savings.

evidence.claim: GXO reports that new customers/sites require time, operational focus and capital; some warehouse infrastructure costs are recovered over the customer relationship, exposing unrecovered capital to default. It identifies bidding, pricing, service quality and customer insourcing as competitive constraints.
evidence.locator: Item 1A, competition, new-customer onboarding and customer-default risk paragraphs
evidence.limitations: Qualitative risk disclosure, not measured newco CAC, default frequency or rollout delay. It establishes mechanisms to model rather than numerical coefficients.

evidence.claim: ISS says it is deploying more than 800 sweep/vacuum/scrub robots across 21 countries and using a site-specific Cobot Framework covering justification, robot selection and privacy. Its digital scheduling uses activity sensors and user requests.
evidence.observation_period: Deployment program described as of publication; exposure window undisclosed
evidence.locator: From routine to responsive and Cobots and cleaners subsections
evidence.limitations: Deploying is not a verified count of retained productive robots. No site-level exposure, hardware/software mix, costs or counterfactual controls. The US cell uses global evidence as a structural comparator, not a US deployment denominator.

evidence.claim: ISS reports 30% improved floor-cleaning efficiency at multiple UK customer sites, while describing human assessment and additional cleaning after robot work.
evidence.locator: Cobots and cleaners, paragraph beginning The devices also reduce physical strain
evidence.limitations: Efficiency numerator, denominator, baseline, sample size and paid-hours removal are not disclosed. Do not use 30% as a US labor saving, total-facility productivity estimate or humanoid coefficient.

evidence.claim: Tennant and Brain announced an exclusive next-generation floorcare technology agreement, a bundled equipment/autonomy offer sold by Tennant and recurring autonomy revenue for Tennant. Tennant disclosed a $32 million investment and a board seat.
evidence.observation_period: Agreement announced 2024-02-22; X4 launch then planned for Q2 2024
evidence.locator: Opening bullets; X4 ROVR paragraph; paragraph beginning With this agreement and starting; final investment paragraph
evidence.limitations: Exclusivity concerns specified next-generation floorcare technology, not every Brain product or a universal robotics monopoly. No fee split, customer prices, margins, asset title or realized ROI disclosed.

evidence.claim: ABM describes monthly fixed-price, square-foot, cost-plus, hourly and transaction-price service contracts. Most contracts are cancellable without a substantive penalty, with a majority requiring 30–90 days notice.
evidence.locator: Note 2, Contracts with Customers; Contract Types subsections
evidence.limitations: Company-wide disclosure, not a robot purchase/lease contract or proof that every cleaning contract has the same cancellation right. High historical retention and short contractual notice can coexist.

evidence.claim: The retrieved BrainOS/Kärcher agreement licenses rather than sells software, ties use to service access, leaves operational-data ownership with the end user, and grants Brain a perpetual nonexclusive improvement-use license. Operational-data export is governed by subscription provisions rather than automatically assured by ownership. Personal data is excluded from the operational-data definition; aggregated data not linked to the end user is also excluded from defined Operational Data under section 5.2.
evidence.observation_period: Retrieved artifact; applicable effective term is contract-specific
evidence.geography: Kärcher North America contracting form; territorial and legal applicability subject to agreement
evidence.limitations: Filename suggests 2-2025 while extracted document title identifies v2021_12; effective date unresolved. This is an available standard form, not an executed ISS/Tennant/GXO contract. Do not transfer rights to other products. Improvement permission is not proof that data improves models or produces exclusive gains. End-user ownership must therefore be interpreted within the defined data category, not extended automatically to aggregated unlinked data.
evidence.publication_date_missingness_reason: No reliable publication/effective date established from retrieved document.
evidence.artifact_version: Filename kira-b100-eula-2-2025.pdf; extracted title EULA_Karcher Subscription Agreement v2021_12; conflict unresolved

evidence.claim: OpenAI announced an ownership stake and embedded research/product/engineering collaboration with Thrive Holdings, initially focused on accounting and IT services. Thrive is described as investing in, acquiring and building businesses.
evidence.limitations: Ownership stake size, detailed governance, exclusivity, data rights, cash terms and realized productivity not provided. Digital services comparator only; no physical-deployment economics established.

evidence.claim: Thrive announced more than $2 billion new capital at a $12 billion valuation, more than $3 billion cumulative capital raised and more than 70 owned/operated businesses; it describes embedded engineers and a new built-environment technical/regulatory services platform.
evidence.limitations: Financing and operating counts are issuer claims. No audited platform returns, quantified causal AI savings, asset financing terms, or humanoid deployments. A new parent/platform is not necessarily new underlying productive capacity.

evidence.claim: Hadrian announced $260 million new capital, a factory expansion loan arrangement and planned Arizona manufacturing expansion; it described an operating Torrance factory, proprietary Opus software and factories-as-a-service.
evidence.observation_period: Operating Torrance footprint at announcement; Arizona/full-operation timing forward-looking
evidence.locator: Opening financing paragraphs, Arizona bullet, Opus paragraph and About Hadrian
evidence.limitations: Disclosure language is ambiguous on the split of equity and loan facility: do not add $260m to an assumed loan amount. No verified utilization, profitability, realized ramp date or common-technology causal comparison. Proprietary software and defense-market conditions limit analogy to an off-the-shelf humanoid operator.

evidence.claim: Brain reports an unnamed grocery retailer deployment across more than 100 locations, with 33,649 labor hours reallocated in 2024 and over $2.1m annual value.
evidence.locator: How did a leading grocery retailer transform store operations with automation?
evidence.limitations: Vendor case with unnamed customer, unreported robot exposure and unavailable value methodology. Reallocated time is not payroll eliminated. The implied value/hour must not be treated as a wage or independent cash saving. Kept as qualified supporting/counterevidence, not calibration.

evidence.claim: ISS announced a three-year European cleaning-service expansion effective July 2025, using existing customer knowledge across three countries.
evidence.limitations: Unnamed customer; termination options, pricing, robot use and gain-sharing are undisclosed. Stated nominal duration is not proof of guaranteed robot-cost recovery.

evidence.claim: GXO reports completing the Wincanton acquisition in April 2024, with June 2025 competition approval conditional on divesting certain UK grocery contracts.
evidence.limitations: This is an actual logistics acquisition/control constraint, not evidence that the acquisition was AI-native or that it created extra underlying service activity. No acquisition automation return is inferred.

fixed_baseline: same layout and direct operating resource requirements
comparisons.conclusion: Fixed-price 3PL can retain cost improvement until repricing; cost-plus may pass savings to shipper. In-house owner avoids the external margin split but must supply integration and operating capability. No general winner from ownership alone.
comparisons.counterevidence: GXO is already adopting and investing; a presumed slow incumbent is not the only relevant comparator.

fixed_baseline: same accessible floor and cleanliness standard
same retained human setup/review and supplies
varied_mechanisms: ability to redeploy asset across sites
comparisons.conclusion: A contractor can pool assets and support but bears contract-loss/redeployment risk; an owner-operator can align asset and building horizon but may lack implementation capacity. Short termination notice can dominate low upfront RaaS pricing.
comparisons.counterevidence: Service operators already deploy specialized robots; reallocated hours and vendor annual value are not evidence of payroll removal.

analogy_tests.source_population: Owned digital-service businesses and embedded AI engineering platform
analogy_tests.target_population: Physical-service operating newcos, acquisitions and hybrid platform
analogy_tests.mechanism: Aligned operational authority, capital allocation and embedded deployment teams can reduce organization/interface frictions.
required_similarities: reusable engineering with sufficient domain overlap
ability to retain gains and fund ramp
analogy_tests.prediction: Platform benefit should appear in lower all-in deployment cost or faster repeatable operation net of central overhead, at matched accepted output.
analogy_tests.falsifier: Standalone firms or prompt incumbents match outcomes while platform overhead, integration burden or funding concentration consume the savings.
analogy_tests.permitted_model_use: Qualitative mechanism structure only; no transferred valuation, adoption rate, return or robot-cost coefficient.

analogy_tests.source_population: Funded proprietary manufacturing operator selling physical output
analogy_tests.target_population: Customer newco using widely accessible humanoids
analogy_tests.mechanism: Operating business can bundle equity and factory financing to form physical capacity and sell outcomes.
material_differences: specific manufacturing process versus general service
analogy_tests.prediction: Target must demonstrate bankable or equity-financeable demand and ramp milestones independent of AI branding.
analogy_tests.falsifier: No customer commitment or finance at viable terms despite positive assumed unit contribution.
analogy_tests.permitted_model_use: Existence of financing/formation pathway and questions only; no borrowed capital availability or productivity coefficient.

model_constraints.statement: Keep customer ownership/organization, robot asset title, commercial terms and model/data rights as separate dimensions.

An annual fixed-price service, cost-plus contract and hourly billing can retain different portions of the same physical productivity benefit; calculate from the explicit contract, never a label multiplier.
RaaS/customer cash relief creates provider or financier investment and service obligations; no system-wide capex disappearance. Include early termination and asset redeployability.
Data ownership must not automatically grant export, exclusivity, training rights, transfer effectiveness or a second additive data premium.
Keep incumbent same-robot response and moving digital-only/specialized baselines. Incumbents have observed adoption and can compete through bundled service, pricing and installed relationships.
Reallocated time and reported customer value are not measured payroll savings. Demand and service quality determine whether capacity becomes paid revenue.

questions.decision_consequence: Whether newco survives and whether service contracts can fund deployment
questions.evidence_target: Matched customer contract cancellation/renewal, pricing, payment lag, rollout outlays, supplier RaaS fee and termination terms
questions.next_action: Search public procurement contracts and disclosed leases for a matched physical-service case; then compare positive margin with minimum financing need.
questions.stopping_condition: One coherent contract/cash boundary with adverse termination and equal-technology response; leave unavailable parameters explicit.

questions.decision_consequence: Who can authorize a deployment and retain gains
questions.evidence_target: Two matched adopter cohorts holding workload and system fixed, with observed approval/implementation time and retention of savings
questions.next_action: Seek buyer-side capital-policy and pilot-to-rollout disclosures; do not use legal ownership as instrument for adoption.
questions.stopping_condition: A comparison with measured mechanism or explicitly unresolved causal identification.

questions.decision_consequence: Feasible learning network and provider/customer lock-in
questions.evidence_target: Executed humanoid contract or authoritative model/data terms, plus actual export and reuse rights
questions.next_action: Locate public Digit/other deployment terms; compare with artifact-specific BrainOS terms without transferring them.
questions.stopping_condition: Collect/store/access/export/train/redistribute/commercialize rights assigned separately to named actors.

questions.decision_consequence: Build, acquire, platform or hybrid choice
questions.evidence_target: Acquisition price and transformation capex; customer retention and cash generation; standalone greenfield comparator
questions.next_action: Trace one operator acquisition and one pure operating-newco ramp, separating announced from productive capacity.
questions.stopping_condition: Scenario threshold at which purchased customer access/engineering saves more than premium, legacy transition and overhead.

questions.decision_consequence: Durability of entry advantage and value capture after convergence
questions.evidence_target: Renewal prices, multi-vendor switching, same-robot incumbent adoption and support-density economics
questions.next_action: Seek repeat contract cohorts and competition disclosures, including failed pilots and lost customers.
questions.stopping_condition: Evidence distinguishing persistent operating advantage from transient timing and selected pilot success.
